text:
Zoe: weird one this morning Morning folks :construction: 
Zoe: my upstairs neighbor started drilling at 8:30 and apparently their hammer/power-tools rattled my wall so hard my cheap bookshelf slid, knocking my webcam off the tripod and unplugging the ethernet behind the desk. tragic but also comedy. pic: /files/desk_mess.jpg
Ben: yikes. tripod footage? :joy: hope the USB connector survived.
Claire: that stinks. did Windows/Linux even see the camera after replug? sometimes USB enumerates weird after a wobble.
Zoe: Laptop shows the camera disconnected; unplug/replug nothing. USB-C hub light blinks. tried different hub port and it works 944d09
Omar: quick hardware checklist: swap cable, try direct to laptop, try a different port, `lsusb` or Device Manager to see if camera is recognized.
Hana: fwiw i taped my tripod to the desk after a cat incident. duct tape is underrated. also, cheap webcams have tiny solder joints that decouple, so a wiggle can kill them.
Zoe: tried `lsusb` shows nothing for the camera. `dmesg | tail` shows `usb 1-3: device descriptor read/64, error -32` a few times. suspects hardware. will test another camera later.
Ben: if it's just the hub, a power-cycle or switching to a powered USB hub might help. if you need a camera for meetings, i can lend my spare Logitech C270 via porch drop (close to you?)
Zoe: omg that would save me. could i pick up later? also filed a noise complaint with the building; contractor said sorry but needs to finish drywall.
Claire: on the networking side, did the ethernet come back after you nudged the cables? sometimes connectors partially back out when jostled.
Zoe: ethernet link light was off. reseated RJ45, now link solid, but noticed 100mbps instead of gig. `ethtool eth0` shows negotiated 100baseT full. pulled the cable and it's a little bent near the clip. maybe the strain damaged pairs.
Omar: try another cable and port. if it's still 100mbps, try forcing autoneg off? safer to swap the cable first. `sudo ethtool -s eth0 speed 1000 duplex full autoneg on` (if hardware supports) but prefer replacing cable.
Hana: status-bot: reminder to folks --- status-bot: office-safety reminder: secure loose monitors, tripods, and cabling. submit expense for replacement webcam under Home Office Equipment if needed. ---
Zoe: thanks status-bot. also did a quick perf check over hotspot: latency fine but upload limited. will try the spare cable now.
Ben: also pro tip: keep a tiny travel webcam in a drawer for the day a device dies. they are $15 and life-saving.
Claire: also if you end up replacing the camera, consider a small clamp-mount instead of tripod less desk real estate.
Omar: any dust or glass shards? i know this is silly but had a cracked lens once after a book drop. handle with gloves.
Zoe: all good, no glass. new cable fixed gig link. camera is probably toast, but i can use Ben's spare for now. thanks y'all 
Hana: glad it's mostly sorted. feel free to ping for porch logistics Ben.
Zoe: appreciate it. will post a calmer desk photo later (current chaos = "before") :camera_with_flash:
